findings.evidence: Perfect.lean:67-68 `unipotent_zero_mem_commutator (hn : n ≠ 0) (b : ...) : unipotent n 0 b ∈ ⁅suzukiGroup n, suzukiGroup n⁆` vs Perfect.lean:83-84 `unipotent_mem_commutator (hn : n ≠ 0) (a b : ...) : unipotent n a b ∈ ⁅suzukiGroup n, suzukiGroup n⁆`. All uses are internal: lines 96, 115, 121-122, 130.
findings.fix: Mark `unipotent_zero_mem_commutator`, `unipotent_mem_commutator` and `weyl_mem_commutator` `private` (they are used only within this file, before `commutator_suzukiGroup`), and drop the first two from the `## Main results` list at lines 38-39, leaving `commutator_suzukiGroup` and `isPerfect_suzukiGroup` as the file's surface.
findings.issue: `unipotent_zero_mem_commutator hn b` is definitionally the same statement as `unipotent_mem_commutator hn 0 b` (line 83); both are public. Further, once `commutator_suzukiGroup` (line 127) exists, `unipotent_mem_commutator` and `weyl_mem_commutator` are each one rewrite away from `unipotent_mem_suzukiGroup`/`weyl_mem_suzukiGroup`, so all three are strictly weaker restatements of the file's own result.

findings.evidence: mathlib `Mathlib/Algebra/CharP/Two.lean:80-81`: `@[scoped simp] theorem add_self_eq_zero (x : R) : x + x = 0` — scoped, and `Generated.lean:199` itself must write `CharTwo.add_self_eq_zero` by name rather than relying on `simp`.
findings.fix: Remove `@[simp]` from `unipotent_inv`; its only use is the explicit `rw` in Torus.lean:165. (Compare `weyl_inv`/`weyl_mul_weyl` at lines 205-215, which are confluent because `weyl * weyl` does reduce to `1`.)
findings.issue: `@[simp] unipotent_inv` together with `@[simp] unipotent_mul_unipotent` breaks `mul_inv_cancel` for these elements. Simp rewrites the `(unipotent n a b)⁻¹` subterm before trying lemmas at the parent, so `mul_inv_cancel` never matches; `unipotent_mul_unipotent` then produces `unipotent n (a + a) (b + (b + a * a ^ 2 ^ (n+1)) + a * a ^ 2 ^ (n+1))`, which the default simp set cannot reduce to `1` because `CharTwo.add_self_eq_zero` is scoped. A goal `unipotent n a b * (unipotent n a b)⁻¹ = 1` that `simp` closed before is left open.

findings.evidence: `unipotentMatrix` (Generated.lean:103-106) has entry `(1,0) = a` and entry `(3,1) = b`, so injectivity is immediate from `unipotentMatrix_apply` (line 117); grep for `unipotent` across `code/TauCeti` returns no equality-decomposition lemma for `unipotent`.
findings.fix: Add the injectivity/elimination lemma beside the group law, e.g. `theorem unipotent_inj : unipotent n a b = unipotent n c d ↔ a = c ∧ b = d` (with the `@[simp]` `unipotent_eq_one_iff : unipotent n a b = 1 ↔ a = 0 ∧ b = 0` as a corollary of it and `unipotent_zero_zero`).
findings.issue: The PR establishes the group law of `unipotent` (mul, inv, identity) but adds no elimination rule: nothing lets a consumer pass from `unipotent n a b = unipotent n c d` (or `= 1`) back to the parameters. Every consumer of `unipotent_mul_unipotent`, `unipotent_inv` and `commutatorElement_torus_unipotent` can only use them left-to-right; e.g. `⁅torus m κ, unipotent m a b⁆ = 1 ↔ ...` or `suzukiGroup n ≠ ⊥` are out of reach without unfolding to matrices.

summary: Three surface issues: `unipotent_zero_mem_commutator` is an exact special case of `unipotent_mem_commutator` and all three generator-membership lemmas are trivial consequences of the file's own `commutator_suzukiGroup`, so they should be `private`; `@[simp]` on `unipotent_inv` combined with `@[simp]` on `unipotent_mul_unipotent` stops `mul_inv_cancel` from firing on unipotent generators; and the new group-law API has no elimination rule recovering the parameters from an equation of `unipotent` terms.
